title: Uniform residue-field criterion for perfect ring complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $C\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and let $a\leq b$ be integers. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ put $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=R/\mathfrak m$. Assume $H^i(C\otimes_R^L\kappa(\mathfrak m))=0$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$, where derived scalar extension is that of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then $C$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and for every $R$-module $M$ one has $H^i(C\otimes_R^L M)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$.

proof.text: Choose the bounded-above finite-free representative P of C from [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Free modules are flat, so the proved upstream kFlat_of_isStrictlyLE_of_flat applies. QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso and homologyFunctorFactors identify the homology of each C tensor-derived M[0] with ordinary termwise tensor of P and M, using the given derived model isomorphism. This is the degree-zero specialization of [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] and the ordinary K-flat convention [def-pc-module-kflat-complex].

For every i outside [a,b], transfer the maximal residue hypothesis through those homology isomorphisms and apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-residue-tensor-exact] to P at that degree. Transfer its conclusion back to derived tensors. This proves precisely the universal module-tensor vanishing assertion, and isGE_iff and isLE_iff give torAmplitudeIn R a b C.

Apply the already proved [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] to C, its original pseudo-coherence witness, and the interval a<=b just obtained. Its bounded finite-projective representative has termwise vanishing outside some [l,r]; isStrictlyGE_iff and isStrictlyLE_iff turn those bounds into the two support instances in [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Reverse its model isomorphism to obtain IsPerfect C. Pair this with the universal vanishing statement from the preceding step. No local interval cuts or perfect principal-cover gluing are needed.
